expectations.evidence: The rewrite adds "the one bottleneck that mattered" (the original never names a single bottleneck) and "None of this was clever", and it drops the original's note that the 12% to 87% hit rate and the 6-minute test-time cut are the stated outcomes only partly tied to the 41-to-19 result, while also asserting "Most of those 41 minutes" where the original said most time wasn't spent compiling.
The rewrite has no em dashes, cliches or staged reveals; "None of this was clever." is plain, and the only "game changer" is inside the quoted retro line.

Sentence lengths vary and the wording is concrete, as in "They were spent downloading the same dependencies on every run" and "Three of the 11 services accounted for 70% of build time, so we started with those."
It stays an engineering team blog post with sections like "Caching" and "Sharding tests", neither hype nor jokey nor a bare bullet list.
